Our mission at Duolingo is to develop the best education in the world and make it universally available. It’s a big mission, and that’s where you come in!

At Duolingo, you’ll join a team that cares about educating our users, experimenting with big ideas, making fact-based decisions, and finding innovative solutions to complex problems. You’ll have limitless learning opportunities and daily collaborations with world-class minds — while doing work that’s both meaningful and fun.

Join our life-changing mission to develop education for our half a billion (and growing!) learners around the world.

Read our blog to learn more.

About the role...

Join us to build Duolingo Ads, Duolingo’s premium programmatic business. Most learners use our free, ad‑supported app—so great ads are core to our mission. Reporting into the Head of Ad Sales, the Ad Sales Lead, Programmatic will build a deal‑led book of business with agency holding companies, independent agencies, and advertisers who want access to Duolingo’s native formats, first‑party learner signals, and one of the most engaged mobile audiences in the world. You will own buy‑side relationships across holdco investment and programmatic teams, trading desks, curation and principal media groups, and premium programmatic buyers. This is a high‑ownership, high‑visibility, early‑stage opportunity to help define how programmatic can fuel high‑quality ads for millions of learners while driving outcomes for partners.

🧠 You will...

• Own a programmatic revenue target and forecast, and build a predictable pipeline across agency holding‑company programmatic and investment teams, trading desks, independent agencies, and premium programmatic buyers.

• Lead our shift from open auction to premium, deal‑led PMP/PG by packaging Duolingo’s native formats and first‑party learner signals into always‑on and custom deals that buyers will pay a premium for, and negotiate annual and upfront commitments that make that revenue durable.

• Become the person holdco programmatic teams call about mobile app inventory: run joint business planning; get Duolingo onto preferred supply paths, curated marketplaces, and principal/outcome‑based buys; and defend our position when buyers consolidate

• Build the programmatic value proposition and measurement story through proposals, pricing narratives, and post‑campaign proof that connect our native formats and audience data to brand and performance outcomes (e.g., verification, attention, brand lift, incrementality, MMM).

• Partner with Ad Platform Operations and Ad Ops on deal setup, targeting, floors, pacing, and troubleshooting—ensuring what you sell is deliverable and delivers against expectations.

• Work alongside our direct sellers under clear rules of engagement so programmatic expands the account through incremental value; coordinate with Account Management pre‑ and post‑sale to drive renewal and expansion.

• Feed structured market intelligence back to sales, product, and engineering leadership about what buyers need in pricing, packaging, audience segments, formats, and integrations, balancing this input with our learner‑first standards and operational quality.

• Establish the operating rhythm for a scaling programmatic business via account planning, outreach cadences, deal hygiene in CRM, pipeline rigor, and repeatable playbooks the next sellers can run.

✅ You have...

• 8+ years in digital advertising, including at least 4 years selling programmatic on the sell side (publisher/platform/app) or in a holding‑company programmatic/investment role, carrying and hitting a quota; demonstrated PMP/PG selling and trading‑desk engagement.

• A demonstrated book of PMP and PG business you personally sourced, negotiated, and grew.

• Experience selling premium mobile or consumer app inventory—especially video and native/custom formats—through programmatic channels to top‑tier advertisers and agencies.

• Strong understanding of ad tech and mobile app ecosystems, including DSP/SSP workflows, deal IDs, verification/measurement, and using data to inform pricing and packaging.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills; clear, concise storytelling for both technical and non‑technical audiences.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Deep, current relationships with programmatic leads at major agency holding companies and larger independents.

• Experience moving partners from a heavy open‑auction mix to meaningful always‑on/custom PMP/PG alongside direct sales—and knowing what actually moved the deal (packaging, pricing, supply path, or sales motion).

• Sold against first‑party audience segments or custom data products, not just inventory.

• Hands‑on partnership with Ad Ops on deal setup, SSP onboarding, and campaign QA to improve fill, CPMs, and delivery quality.

As the Proctor Quality and Learning Manager (L3) in Scaling Operations, you will own the end-to-end quality standard and learning system that keep our global proctor network aligned and effective as security threats, technology, and workflows evolve. You’ll define what “correct” looks like, run our calibration and adjudication program, and build ongoing training that measurably improves decision quality. You will partner with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering to ensure our human and AI-assisted workflows meet rigorous accuracy standards before and after deployment. This is an individual-contributor role within DET Proctoring Operations, with functional leadership over Training Specialists and adjudicators executing the program.

🧠 You will...

• Own the DET proctoring quality standard — maintain rubrics, decision rules, examples, and guidance that define accurate decisions across routine and difficult edge cases.

• Lead calibration and adjudication — operate recurring Proctor Certification Test cycles, resolve disputed decisions, identify patterns of disagreement, and ensure outcomes are consistent and auditable.

• Build and run an ongoing learning program — publish a forward-looking training calendar, deliver monthly interventions, and launch targeted training in response to quality signals, threats, or workflow changes.

• Measure effectiveness — use calibration results, audits, and performance trends to identify learning needs, evaluate training impact, and decide when to clarify standards, retrain, or update guidance.

• Guide specialist execution — set expectations for Training Specialists and adjudicators, assign deliverables, review outputs, and operate onboarding and certification that ramp new specialists quickly.

• Maintain durable sources of truth — keep calibration, adjudication, and training runbooks current so critical processes are documented and auditable.

• Evolve quality alongside proctoring — translate new threats and workflow changes into clear standards, training, and quality controls in partnership with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering.

• Represent the proctoring craft — bring frontline proctor evidence into product experiments and workflow decisions; assess whether launched changes preserve decision quality.

• Connect human and technology-assisted quality — establish benchmarks for AI-assisted workflows and validate automated capabilities against real sessions before deployment.

✅ You have...

• 5+ years in assessment development, scoring/rater quality, certification, quality assurance, or a field involving complex, consequential judgments; experience aligning reviewers to a shared standard through calibration programs.

• Adult-learning program experience spanning onboarding, certification, ongoing training, remediation, and effectiveness measurement (beyond one-off materials).

• Exceptional attention to detail and strong judgment in ambiguous cases; ability to produce clear, defensible decisions and guidance.

• Analytical fluency to interpret quality data, disagreement patterns, and performance trends and translate them into practical interventions.

• Clear written and verbal communication; ability to turn complex standards into precise, usable guidance and explain difficult calls.

• Cross-functional leadership without formal authority; experience directing contractors or partners toward clear accountability and outcomes.

• Demonstrated skill in quality standards and rubric design, building living systems with decision logs, change histories, and controls for auditability.

• Experience defining quality benchmarks and validation methods for human–technology workflows, including AI-assisted processes.

• Adaptability — comfort revising standards and programs as risks, products, and technology change.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Experience in language assessment, test security, remote proctoring, trust and safety, or fraud prevention in high-integrity environments.

• Experience maintaining quality across large, distributed examiner/rater/reviewer/contractor populations.

• Familiarity with assessment concepts such as inter-rater agreement, reliability, standardization, and performance monitoring.

• Experience designing quality systems that span human judgment and technology-assisted workflows.

• Familiarity with learning-management systems, assessment platforms, quality-audit tools, or operational analytics.

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

Watershed is a software platform for running a world-class climate program. We measure our success in the carbon reduction achievements of our customers. We are looking for team members to join our team focused on delivering outcomes for our Financial Institution customers.

You’ll work on the team turning Watershed’s data layer into an intelligence platform: BI-grade querying, AI-powered discovery and analysis, and the schema architecture underneath it all. The goal is for customers to get answers inside Watershed—not export to Excel.

What you could work on:

• Build new interactive data visualizations to help climate leads understand their company's emissions.

• Build APIs to unify carbon data access for customers and other engineers.

• Build tools that help financial institutions measure and report emissions across their portfolio companies.

• Build tools for customers to effectively ingest and interpret business data.

You will:

• Ship code to production on day one

• Collaborate with product, design, climate science, and data science to build and iterate on software that helps our customers understand their climate data

You might be a fit if you:

• Have 6+ years of software engineering industry experience, preferably in Node.js web development or data pipelines

• Have experience building scalable software starting from user needs

• Are excited to join a startup and are ready to help evolve a growing engineering team

This role will be based in our New York City office.

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

What if I need accommodations for my interview?

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

We offer creators a variety of ways to engage with their fans and build a lasting business including: paid memberships, free memberships, community chats, live video, and selling to fans directly with one-time purchases.

Ultimately our goal is simple: fund the creative class. And we're leaders in that space, with:

• $10 billion+ generated by creators since Patreon's inception

• 100 million+ free memberships for fans who may not be ready to pay just yet, and

• 25 million+ paid memberships on Patreon today.

We're continuing to invest heavily in building the best creator platform with the best team in the creator economy and are looking for a Staff Software Engineer, Data Infrastructure to support our mission.

This role is remote, with optional in-person attendance in either the New York or San Francisco office.

About the Team

The Data Foundations team at Patreon builds the pipelines, models, and infrastructure that power both customer-facing and internal data products. The Data Infrastructure function within the team owns the foundational platform — streaming, batch, and data lake infrastructure — that every data pipeline, analytics workload, and ML system at Patreon runs on.

You'll join a small, high-craft team that partners across Product, Data Science, Infrastructure, and the rest of Engineering to make sure the platform underneath all of that work is reliable, scalable, and easy for other engineers to build on.

About the Role

• Architect, build, and operate large scale batch and streaming platforms that directly power Patreon product features, analytics, and experimentation.

• Stand up and scale event-driven and streaming systems (Kafka, Kinesis, PubSub, or similar) for real-time data ingestion, transformation, aggregation, and delivery to different data storage systems.

• Build self-serve data platforms that let engineers, data scientists, and analysts safely discover data, define contracts, and create and operate pipelines with minimal friction.

• Partner with the broader Infrastructure, Platform, and product engineering to drive architectural decisions across storage, compute, deployment, and orchestration to align the data ecosystem with Patreon’s roadmap.

• Build the tooling, monitoring, and observability that gives engineers confidence in the data platform's reliability and performance.

• Mentor other engineers on infrastructure and streaming best practices, and help shape the long-term data infrastructure roadmap.

What you'll need:

• 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 4+ years focused on data or platform infrastructure.

• Deep, hands-on experience architecting both batch (Airflow, Dagster, or similar) and stream processing systems at scale (Spark, Flink, Kafka Streams, or similar).

• Familiarity with data quality, lineage, observability, and governance tooling.

• Strong programming skills in Python (Java, Scala, or Go a plus) and SQL.

• Familiarity with cloud infrastructure and broad fluency across data stores: Object storage (S3), RDMS (MySQL, or Postgres, etc.), Key value (DynamoDB), OLAP (Clickhouse, Pinot, or Druid, etc.), search/indexing (Elasticsearch) plus data flow patterns for keeping them in sync with source systems.

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills; comfortable driving cross-functional infrastructure decisions.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or the equivalent.

Bonus if you have:

• Experience with Delta Lake/Iceberg, AWS, or Databricks.

• Contributed to open-source streaming or infrastructure tooling.

• Experience supporting ML/AI workflows, training pipelines, or evaluation systems.

We hire talented and passionate people from different backgrounds because workplace diversity and inclusion is critical to our ability to serve creators worldwide. If you’re excited about a role but your past experience doesn’t match with every bullet point outlined above, we strongly encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re a creator at heart, are energized by our mission, and share our company values, we’d love to hear from you.

Patreon powers creators to do what they love and get paid by the people who love what they do. Our team is passionate about making this mission and our core values come to life every day in our work. Through this work, our Patronauts:

We offer creators a variety of ways to engage with their fans and build a lasting business including: paid memberships, free memberships, community chats, live video, and selling to fans directly with one-time purchases.

Ultimately our goal is simple: fund the creative class. And we're leaders in that space, with:

• $10 billion+ generated by creators since Patreon's inception

• 100 million+ free memberships for fans who may not be ready to pay just yet, and

• 25 million+ paid memberships on Patreon today.

We're continuing to invest heavily in building the best creator platform with the best team in the creator economy and are looking for a Software Engineer, Backend to support our mission.

This role is based in New York or San Francisco and open to those who are able to be in-office 3 days per week on a hybrid work model.

About the Team

Our team builds the insights and analytics experiences creators rely on to understand and grow their business on Patreon, along with the infrastructure that keeps those numbers accurate and trustworthy. We partner closely with Data Engineering, Data Science, Product, and Design to turn creator and fan data into features creators use every day.

About the Role

As a Backend Engineer on the team, you will build and own the services, APIs, and data flows behind creator insights. You will bring a strong backend foundation and the curiosity to work in the data layer: designing data models, building and maintaining pipelines and jobs, and making sure the data creators see is correct, fast, and reliable. You will work across the stack from ingestion to the product surface, and take on work that today depends heavily on Data Engineering.

In this role you will:

• Design, build, and operate backend services and APIs that serve creator insights at scale.

• Build and maintain data pipelines, jobs, and models that feed insights features, in partnership with Data Engineering.

• Improve data quality, monitoring, and performance so creators can trust what they see.

• Collaborate with product managers, designers, data scientists, and engineers to turn ambiguous questions into well-scoped solutions.

• Drive technical design, write well-tested and maintainable code, and mentor teammates.

What you’ll need:

• 3+ years or 5+ years of experience in backend software development, building production services and APIs.

• Strong programming skills in Python or a similar language, with good engineering practices (testing, CI/CD, monitoring).

• Strong SQL skills and experience designing and optimizing relational data models (e.g. MySQL, PostgreSQL).

• Hands-on experience with data-intensive work, such as batch or streaming pipelines, scheduled jobs, event logging, or serving analytical data (e.g. Airflow, Spark, Kafka / Kinesis, dbt, a data lake or warehouse).

• Care about data accuracy and reliability, including idempotency, backfills, and handling late or duplicate data.

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills; comfortable partnering with product, design, and data teams.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or the equivalent.

Bonus if you have:

• Experience with data quality, lineage, or observability tooling.

• Experience building customer-facing analytics, reporting, or insights features.

• Familiarity with metric design and data modeling for analytics and experimentation.

• Familiarity with Elastic Search or OLAP

We hire talented and passionate people from different backgrounds because workplace diversity and inclusion is critical to our ability to serve creators worldwide. If you’re excited about a role but your past experience doesn’t match with every bullet point outlined above, we strongly encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re a creator at heart, are energized by our mission, and share our company values, we’d love to hear from you.

About Patreon

Patreon powers creators to do what they love and get paid by the people who love what they do. Our team is passionate about making this mission and our core values come to life every day in our work. Through this work, our Patronauts:

• Put Creators First | They’re the reason we’re here. When creators win, we win.

• Build with Craft | We sign our name to every deliverable, just like the creators we serve.

• Make it Happen | We don’t quit. We learn and deliver.

• Win Together | We grow as individuals. We win as a team.

Patreon is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We provide employment opportunities without regard to age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any other protected class. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the interview process, please let us know via email at accommodations@patreon.

Job Description:

The New York Times' Advertising team is looking for an Analyst, Measurements and Insights who is experienced in analysis of campaign performance data and campaign stories for clients advertising. You will support the Measurement team within The New York Times Advertising. You will turn campaign results into applicable findings for clients by using first- and third-party campaign metrics. You will help identify opportunities, bring the strategy and ongoing output of insights, innovate processes, methodologies, and reporting, directly affecting future business.
This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Manager, Insights and Analytics. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role:

You will evolve how we measure media and creative across a portfolio of diverse clients. This collaborative and strategic role will work with top tier advertising clients. You will also work with multiple teams, including Sales, Sales Planning, Ad Product, Audience Insights, Product Marketing, and Strategy teams. This collaboration ensures success with strengthening partnerships with marketers and increasing ad revenue.

Responsibilities:

• Build holistic narratives from large, integrated data sets using data visualization and analytics platforms

• Work with 3rd party vendors in the setup and delivery of campaign effectiveness reports, such as Brand Lift Studies, Attribution and Sales Lift.

• Develop expertise in the full suite of NYT research capabilities and measurement products that deliver main performance metrics across the full marketing funnel, to current and potential clients.

• Collaborate with Strategy to ensure initial campaign goals and client's desired outcomes are incorporated into all post-campaign outputs.

• Identify and recommend ad products to advertiser goals and KPIs based on relevant performance data.

• Be a subject matter expert and provide a high level of service when coordinating and communicating in-depth reporting to clients.

• Be a training resource for educating internal Advertising partners about measurement capabilities and results.

• Socialize industry-level measurement findings across all partners

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in statistics, engineering, economics, or related subject

• 3-5 years of insights / analyst experience at a publisher or media/research agency managing advertiser-facing products including ad performance tracking, marketing or digital analytics

• Understanding of ad operations, digital buying and trafficking, and the digital media landscape required.

• Experience in data analysis and interpretation, extracting insights from large datasets, and business case development to guide decisions and improve products

• Familiarity with Google Analytics and web analytics platforms

• Experience with data visualization (e.g., Tableau, DOMO, and Chartio)

• Experience diplomatically navigating complex team member relationships

• Experience prioritizing competing programs, responsibilities, and projects

Preferred Qualifications:

• Technical familiarity with measurement and attribution partners such as Kantar, Nielsen, Comscore, Brand Metrics & ABCS Insights

The New York Times is looking for an analyst who is passionate about promoting security and technology awareness across our newsroom, engineering, and business departments. You will help design technical training and communications throughout the organization, striving to cultivate a company-wide security culture where all employees share responsibility for safeguarding and protecting us.

Based in New York City, this hybrid role involves regular in-person office visits to host group training sessions and individual meetings with staff.

Who are we?

Enterprise Technology enables the people, platforms, and practices that support The New York Times' journalism and business operations. We partner with departments across the company to help employees work securely,, and productively through thoughtful technology solutions. We support the systems and capabilities that keep us running while looking for new ways to reduce friction and improve the daily experience of our workforce.

The Education team's mission is to help our technical and non-technical workforce adopt secure, technology practices through data-driven insights, training, and specialized programming that inspire meaningful behavior change.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

Responsibilities:

• Partner with staff throughout the company to lead personal and group security and technology education sessions.

• Coordinate and lead workshops, events, and training projects focused on information security and IT topics and initiatives.

• Deliver high-touch technical support and 1:1 briefings for all staff, including the newsroom, providing hands-on guidance on digital hygiene, device hardening, and secure communication workflows.

• Craft and distribute routine security updates for specific teams or the entire organization in collaboration with corporate communications.

• Produce instructional resources, including user guides, manuals, video content, and online modules.

• Support user requests and participate in an on-call rotation to address urgent security inquiries.

• Design and implement internal phishing simulation campaigns and remediation programs.

• Manage the logistical and administrative tasks required to schedule and track training projects.

• Report on security engagement metrics from direct interactions, identifying trends to help refine support strategies and harden newsroom defenses.

• Visit several bureaus and office sites to deliver training; expected travel is approximately 10% annually.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

• You will report to the Manager, Information Security

• 2+ years of experience training on topics related to information security (phishing, account security, data security, secure communications) in person and virtually

• Familiarity with basic cybersecurity concepts, including social engineering, common tactics, techniques, and procedures.

• Experience helping people build and understand threat models for themselves and their function or role within an organization.

• Experience with breaking down complex topics to different audiences, including technical and non-technical partners.

• Comfortable with public speaking and adjusting content based on audience response.

• understanding of the audience to produce engaging materials in multiple formats and media, user guides, and gamification elements.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience with phishing platforms.

• Experience with Zendesk or working in a support environment.

• Experience with learning, creating, and integrating new digital technology such as audio, video, social media, and other web-based technologies.

• Experience working with journalists or other high-risk groups.

• Experience working with leadership and management.

• Knowledge of networking basics, including VPNs, travel routers, and secure Wi-Fi configurations.

• Interest in or experience with specialized security hardware (e.g., YubiKeys, encrypted storage).

• Basic data analytics skills.

The New York Times Advertising is hiring for an Art Director to join our T Brand Studio. As an Art Director, you will lead the visual execution of assigned projects. Art Directors do the following: they imagine ways to tell stories visually. They present visual ideas and recommendations internally and to our clients. They find visual reference, specifically relevant to each idea, project, and opportunity. They contribute to and oversee the creation of great mood boards, inspired type treatments, exceptional color palettes, and page layouts.

About the Role

You will oversee the design of presentations which enhance our work, the assembly of excellent paid posts in webflow, the design of impactful print ads, and work with developers internal and external on complex custom projects. You will mentor Designers and Senior Designers, and collaborate with external partners, building relationships and guiding them through insightful feedback to create their best work. This is a hybrid role, reporting to the Director, Design. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

• Contribute to and oversee excellent design work on client and internal projects, with guidance from Design Directors, and Creative Directors.

• Translate conceptual and strategic ideas into impactful visual solutions.

• Contribute creative concepts to client and internal projects, brainstorming with other teams.

• Design iteratively with an easy command of typography, composition, messaging hierarchy, layout, and other fundamental principles of graphic design, and give pointed feedback to designers which directly improves their work.

• Research and oversee selection of visual reference that inspires (Design, Page Animation, Illustration, and Photography), and build a mental reference library of styles, approaches, creators, and projects.

• Manage Designers, delegate work to resourced Designers and Senior Designers based on workload, capabilities, and experience. Contribute to the professional growth of direct reports through mentorship, and feedback.

• Select, brief, and direct outside collaborators to create their best work.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

• 5+ years of professional work experience in the art industry

• 5+ years of experience with Adobe Creative Cloud (InDesign, Photoshop, Illustrator, Figma) and modern digital publishing platforms such as Webflow.

• An experienced creative portfolio demonstrating mastery of design principles - specifically typography, grid systems, layout hierarchy, color theory, and art direction for both digital and print media

• Experienced managing designers including delegating tasks, giving constructive feedback, and overseeing visual quality.

• Experience commissioning and directing external creative partners including photographers, illustrators, animators and external development teams

• Experience presenting visual strategies and creative direction to executive-level clients and company partners.

• Visual research skills, with a rich, active mental library of contemporary and historical art, design, photography, and interactive digital trends.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Working knowledge of front-end web technologies (HTML/CSS) and an understanding of dynamic layout capabilities, responsive design, and digital motion/animation principles.

• Experience in luxury, editorial, or prestige brand storytelling, with a deep appreciation for high-end aesthetic stewardship and cultural context.

• Experience prioritizing competing programs, responsibilities, and projects

• Knowledge of the top creatives working in the fields of art, photography, and video.

The Well desk is seeking a Deputy Editor to join its core leadership team to oversee editorial operations, including day-to-day scheduling, long-term planning and managing editors and reporters.

You'll push Well editors and reporters to collaborate internally and with the newsroom, and help guide inter-desk collaboration. You will do first edits on stories and top-read our report. You will also serve as the desk deputy and can run all aspects of the desk as a proxy for the Editor of Well, when necessary.

You will report to the Well desk's Editor. This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

• Oversee all aspects of the editorial workflow, including story presentation and promotion. Monitor the status of articles, photography, video and design, as well as display and social copy and any multimedia elements.

• Serve as the primary liaison between Well's desk head and the Well Visuals Team.

• In partnership with the desk head, lead and shape coverage for the desk; make publishing decisions and take ownership of what is published; set the editorial calendar, make sure that all editorial content is on track, and make adjustments when necessary.

• In partnership with the desk head, support team development, culture and morale; accountable for success and development of direct reports and their respective teams.

• In partnership with the desk head, shape and drive desk strategy; identify opportunities for innovation and collaboration.

• Help the desk head to set audience goals and drive the team toward success. Collaborate closely with the desk audience editor.

• Serve as a hiring manager and ensure that hiring decisions follow fair and equitable practices.

• Manage a team of editors and reporters.

• Run the desk's public representation and communications within the greater news organization, with a particular emphasis on helping us play in the big stories of the day Clearly communicate the desk's plans to other desks and stakeholders.

• Lead the effort in defining editorial franchises and lanes of coverage.

• Work closely with Well's operations manager on budget, payroll, freelance contracts and vacation scheduling.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

• 10+ years of experience as an editor, ideally with experience across many forms of storytelling, from news to investigations, features and visual projects.

• Experience with framing and elevating stories for the broadest possible audience.

• Experience with brainstorming ideas and coaching reporters, editors and the visual team so they produce their best work.

•
Stay informed about trends in digital advertising, marketing, branding, media, culture and the evolving social media landscape — bringing those insights into your work in an authentic way.

Bring fresh ideas and a spirit of experimentation to how we market our journalism, product experiences and bundles, contributing to a culture of continuous learning on the creative team.

•

A background in subscription, media or content businesses, with familiarity in how brand, product marketing, and performance media work together across the funnel.

Experience working in video editing software and a working knowledge of on set video production for social channels.

The show's format is loose and conversational. Episodes are built around Wesley's exchanges with fellow critics, artists, and cultural figures; at their best they feel real, incisive, intimate, surprising, loose, unpredictable and crackling with on-the-fly cultural criticism. The senior editor will play a key role in refining this format, ensuring that each episode feels cohesive, dynamic, and fun while showcasing the distinct voice and authority that define Wesley's work.

This job is for you if: you are a rigorous editor, a strong producer and an active, generative collaborator — someone who can listen as well as direct. You enjoy the give and take involved in challenging, sharpening, and expanding ideas in real time with a dynamic team. You know and have respect for Wesley's critical voice. You are an experienced and accomplished culture editor/writer/producer/thinker in your own right, someone with ideas about what's going on in the world of movies, TV, books, music, art and more. You have a keen sense of who the interesting critical voices in this landscape are, and a sense of how to program great guests each week. You are well-organized, someone capable of leading a multidisciplinary team through the many overlapping stages of development and production on multiple episodes at a time. You're adept at working within a larger editorial system, taking notes and other input. You have an understanding of YouTube and other social platforms where the show may travel. You have a feel for the right way to use audience data to inform editorial decision-making. You're adaptable, friendly, creative, and discerning. And above all, you're interested in and capable of doing all the work—both the glamorous and exciting stuff and the basic but necessary stuff—to build a successful show.

As senior editor of Cannonball, you will also be part of the staff of The New York Times Magazine, where Wesley is a staff writer and where the show is based. You will draw on and be part of the magazine's cultural coverage.

• Manage and mentor a multidisciplinary team, setting clear expectations, providing feedback, and fostering a collaborative, high-performing culture.

• Oversee production timelines and workflows, ensuring deadlines are met without compromising quality or ambition.

• Maintain a strong, consistent editorial voice while pushing the show to expand creatively and reach new audiences.

• Develop new formats and concepts for a show that's still evolving.

• Work with Magazine leadership to integrate the show into the Magazine's editorial plans, voice and design, helping the show grow into a recurring, high‑impact Magazine franchise.

• Partner with audience, analytics, and platform teams to understand viewer and listener behavior and refine the show's format, distribution, and growth strategy.

• Work cross-functionally with other newsroom desks and teams to identify opportunities for collaboration, guest booking, and editorial alignment.

• Work proactively with Legal and Standards departments to keep the show free of corrections and/or legal challenges.

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

The Times is looking for reporters with a local story idea who want to investigate it under the editing guidance of Dean Baquet, The Times’s former executive editor, and a group of veteran investigative editors.

The goal of the Local Investigative Fellowship is to provide fellows the opportunity to learn the ways and means of investigative reporting from some of the best in the business. Our fellows will be based in the communities where they are reporting and make periodic trips to The Times’s offices for training and support.

This one year program is for reporters in local newsrooms or freelancers.

Responsibilities:

• Spend a year producing signature investigative work focused on your state or region that will be published by The Times.

• Under the guidance of Mr. Baquet and a handpicked group of veteran editors, you will receive the rare opportunity to learn the judgment, skills and techniques needed to excel at investigative journalism from the best in the business.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

• 3 to 5 years of professional experience as a reporter covering a beat for a local newspaper or local digital news outlet

• You are an independent journalist or a journalist employed at a newsroom willing to provide a yearlong sabbatical

Preferred Qualifications:

• Significant experience covering a beat and an idea for an investigative story that you have not had the time, resources or editing support to pursue

• Ability to bring a new perspectives to investigative journalism

Learn more about the program here .

To apply, upload a résumé, Cover Letter (as described below) and five clips in one attachment. Applications that fail to include any of these materials or follow these instructions will not be considered.

Your Cover Letter must include at least one story idea or pitch, but you may include multiple if you'd like. Please limit each story idea or pitch to 500 words. We are not looking for polished story ideas or pitches. Instead, your answers to these questions will help us assess where you are in the reporting process and what editorial support and resources the local investigative fellowship could offer you.

• What is your investigative story idea or area of focus? How would your story expose something new, something no one else has already revealed?

• Describe who has been harmed and in what way. Is the harm enough to spark outrage?

• Will your story hold someone accountable? Who and how?

• What critical records, data and human sources will be required to tell your story? Describe how you have, or could, obtain these critical sources.

• What do you need help with to report this story, and what are the barriers?

• Can you give us a sense of what has been written about the subject? Please include clips of notable reporting on the topic.

We appreciate proposals that are as detailed as possible. Successful applicants have included specifics about what they aimed to prove through their investigations.

For example, a reporter for The Baltimore Banner had reason to believe that the city’s overdose crisis was the worst in the nation. Mississippi Today had evidence of abuses in local sheriffs offices . And a reporter for The Desert Sun in Palm Springs, Calif., suspected a pattern of deaths inside local jails .

Candidates should submit five published clips that show excellence — in evocative writing, through high-impact news stories and by highlighting the voices of local communities. Your clips should be uploaded to the additional materials application question below. Please ensure to include the full text of your clips, not just the links.

What makes a good local investigation?

• Starts with high stakes
How does the story affect people’s lives and livelihoods? Their health, safety and basic quality of life?

• Has a clear line of accountability
Great investigations have a line of accountability to someone or some group with significant power.

• Reveals something
Does your investigation reveal something that someone or some institution is trying to keep secret?

• Has a clear sense of place
The most important element for any local investigation: How is it (e.g. the policy, the circumstance or the failure) unique to your community?

You may apply to the Local Investigations Fellowship once per calendar year. You may also apply for other newsroom opportunities, however separate applications must be submitted for each program.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. We will not sponsor new work visas for the fellowship, but we may consider you if you have an existing work visa or a valid student visa that can be extended via Optional Practical Training

Applicants will be notified about their status on a rolling basis.

Keep in mind that the fellowships are very competitive and generate a high level of interest. We won’t be able to accept applications that are mailed or emailed to us. Nor will we acknowledge the status of every application upon receipt or during the vetting process. We will contact you for interviews as needed.

These positions are represented by the NewsGuild of NY

The New York Times' Marketing team is looking for a Manager, Event Campaign Production to be the operational engine of the event marketing campaign and production assets. You will oversee the daily creative workflow — from receiving direction from the Director to ensuring the Creative team delivers the right assets, on brief, on brand, and on time. They are the connective tissue between strategy and execution, translating campaign priorities into clear assignments and keeping every moving part accountable. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Director, Event Campaign Strategy and Production. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

About the Role

You will be hands-on, someone who excels at process and clarity. As the Manager, Event Campaign Production, you do not attend external or client-facing partner meetings independently, but operate with authority within the production workflow. You will direct creative output, managing vendor relationships daily, and overseeing the project management infrastructure that keeps the campaign on track.

Responsibilities:

• Be the primary daily point of direction for the Creative team — assigning work, setting task-level priorities, and reviewing output against the brief and brand standards.

• Translate campaign direction from the Director into clear, applicable briefs and assignments for the Creative team and external vendors.

• Build the Marketing Notion Board — the central project management tool tracking all creative tasks, owners, statuses, and deadlines across every active campaign.

• Manage the creative production timeline for each event, from initial brief through final asset delivery.

• Coordinate daily workflow across internal creative teams, external vendors, and agency partners to keep production moving without bottlenecks.

• Brief the NYT Communications Systems team on landing page and event page updates and manage the production timeline for those deliverables.

• Be the primary daily contact for external creative vendors and production agencies, under the strategic direction of the Director and Production Lead.

• Manage the review and approval workflow for all campaign assets — scheduling reviews, coordinating stakeholder feedback, and tracking revisions to completion.

• Manage the timeline, asset coordination, and deliverable tracking for the post-event sizzle reel in collaboration with the Copywriter and Director.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

• 3+ years of experience in creative production, project management, or campaign operations

• 3+ years of experience coordinating review and approval workflows across multiple company partners

• Track record managing complex multi-asset campaigns with many simultaneous moving parts

• Experience briefing and managing external vendors and creative agencies daily

• Process-minded with the instinct to create structure where it is missing

• Working knowledge of the full marketing asset landscape: digital, print, video, social, email, and experiential

Preferred Qualifications:

• Exposure to live event or in-show production

• Experience with events, media, or a marketing environment

• Proficiency with project management tools — Monday.com

The Senior Engineer, Cybersecurity is a hands-on contributor who designs, builds, and operates security controls and services that protect The Times' systems, data, and users. As a member of the Security Architecture team, you will own complex initiatives end-to-end, drive measurable risk reduction, and collaborate across product engineering and enterprise technology with technical depth, operational rigor, and clear communication aligned with business outcomes.

Who are we?

Cybersecurity helps prevent The Times from becoming news. Our teams work to protect the news makers, their support staff, the platforms they rely on every day, as well as all of The Times' products and services, and our readers who consume them.

This role reports to the Director of Engineering, Cybersecurity.

Responsibilities:

• Create an environment that favors context, not control. Empower product engineers and ensure they have the relevant information and tools to deliver secure products and services.

• Design, implement, and operate security controls and services (e.g., identity and access management, secrets management, endpoint/agent hardening, network segmentation, detection, and response automation) that meet reliability, security, scalability, and observability standards.

• Partner with product and platform teams to integrate security into architecture and developer workflows while articulating business impact and tradeoffs.

• Perform security reviews, threat modeling, and risk assessments (code, design, 3rd-party apps).

• Investigate and resolve urgent and/or complex security issues, triaging effectively and driving architectural changes that prevent recurrence.

• Participate via RFCs, community of practices, and other internal knowledge sharing channels to share learnings, align on standards, and influence secure patterns across areas; model The Times' core values in cross-functional collaboration.

• Support team growth through peer design/code review, pairing, and clear feedback; on security engineering practices across the department.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

• 5+ years of experience in software engineering and security engineering space.

• Understanding of security controls across a variety of security domains, including access management, encryption, vulnerability management, AI security, network security, authentication/authorization.

• Knowledge of one or more Cloud platforms (AWS, GCP) and best practices for architecting and securing.

• Experience with software engineering practices (CI/CD, GitOps, IaC, etc.) and related security practices (SAST, SCA, secure by design, shift left, etc.).

• Programming skills in at least one language (Go, Python).

• Experience with containerization and orchestration platforms.

• A bias towards helping people. Many teams will rely on you to help build their systems.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Security/Compliance or DevOps certifications

• Experience with Kubernetes

Lead the technical direction of software delivery as a shared product: shape paved paths in our shared platform that improve code health, release quality, and delivery speed for product teams.

Set the technical direction for agent‑ready delivery: design the policy, guardrails, and paved paths that turn AI‑generated and agent‑driven changes (migrations, test generation, pipeline maintenance) into safe, observable releases at scale by partnering with our Developer AI team.

•
Collaborate with Product, engineering leaders, and internal users to shape the roadmap for the delivery platform and bring measurable impact on quality and speed.

•
Deliver scalable, secure, and observable software delivery systems and workflows that improve reliability, and overall software quality and velocity.

•
Champion engineering excellence in delivery by setting best practices for testing, deployment strategies, progressive delivery, and observability that are easy to adopt through the platform.

•
Mentor engineers across the mission, contribute to hiring, and help foster an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture centered on shared platforms and high‑quality software delivery.

•
Demonstrate support and understanding of our mission and values and a commitment to our purpose to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

•
7+ years of experience building the technical strategy and driving software delivery (Github Actions, Argo CD or equivalent CI/CD systems) or similar platform work with broad organizational impact beyond operations.

Experience building and scaling a platform as a product for internal engineers with multi-tenancy serving many teams through self‑service paved paths, with attention to adoption, backward compatibility, and isolation/guardrails between tenants

•
Demonstrated proficiency in building and maintaining production services in one or more general‑purpose programming languages (e.g., Go, Python, TypeScript/Node.js, or Java), including code review and debugging complex issues.

Liquid Death is looking for a Senior Accounting Clerk who knows that getting the details right keeps the business moving.

In this role, you’ll manage day-to-day accounting transactions with a primary focus on accounts payable. From processing vendor invoices and credits to maintaining accurate records and resolving payment discrepancies, you’ll help ensure our accounting operations run accurately and on time. You’ll also support month-end close by preparing reconciliations, maintaining supporting schedules, and organizing documentation for the accounting team.

You’ll partner closely with Finance, Operations, Sales, and Marketing to obtain approvals, resolve transaction questions, and keep information flowing. You bring strong attention to detail, dependable follow-through, and the ability to manage established workflows independently while recognizing when an issue needs additional review.

We’re also an AI-forward company. We use approved tools like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini to help with recurring, standardized work, then carefully review the outputs. You’ll help identify practical ways to simplify routine tasks while following company requirements for accuracy, confidentiality, and financial controls.

What You’ll Do

Keep accounts payable running smoothly

• Maintain accurate vendor records, including new vendor setup, approved changes, tax forms, and documentation supporting 1099 reporting.

• Process vendor invoices and credits in Tipalti, checking for complete documentation, appropriate coding, required approvals, and duplicate submissions.

• Partner with Operations, Sales, and Marketing to obtain timely invoice reviews, approvals, and supporting information.

• Prepare payment batches and supporting documentation for review and approval in accordance with established controls.

• Respond to vendor inquiries, research invoice and payment discrepancies, and follow through on outstanding credits and balances.

• Prepare AP aging reports and flag overdue items, missing approvals, and other issues requiring follow-up.

• Reconcile vendor statements and assist with AP subledger-to-general-ledger reconciliations, escalating unresolved differences.

Support accounting records and month-end close

• Complete assigned transaction processing and close-support tasks within established deadlines.

• Maintain supporting schedules and documentation for payables, prepaid expenses, and other assigned accounting activities.

• Identify unpaid invoices and gather information to support the accounting team’s preparation of month-end accruals.

• Prepare routine journal entries using established templates and procedures for review and approval by the accounting team.

• Verify account coding and transaction dates against established guidelines, escalating unusual or unclear items.

• Research reconciling differences and help resolve missing, incomplete, or inaccurate transaction records.

Maintain organized records and follow established controls

• Keep invoices, approvals, payment records, reconciliations, and other supporting documents complete and accessible.

• Review transaction reports for missing information, duplicate entries, and other potential errors.

• Retrieve records and prepare supporting documentation for audit, tax, and other accounting requests under the accounting team’s direction.

• Follow established approval procedures and financial controls, promptly flagging exceptions or discrepancies.

• Handle confidential vendor, payment, and business information with discretion.

Improve how the work gets done

• Identify practical ways to improve data accuracy, simplify routine reconciliations, and reduce manual work.

• Assist with testing accounting system updates and changes to established workflows.

• Support responsible use of approved automation and AI tools, verifying outputs before use.

• Maintain clear process documentation and provide backup support for related accounting tasks as needed.

• Proficiency with Excel and Google Sheets, including sorting, filtering, formulas, and lookup functions; familiarity with pivot tables preferred

• Strong attention to detail and the ability to process transactions accurately while managing competing deadlines

• Experience researching invoice, payment, and account discrepancies and following issues through to resolution

• Adaptability and a willingness to learn new systems and improve established processes
